documents.C:
# C

## Purpose

The C module contains the CService implementation in c/service.c. It is the source-level native service surface for this fixture and gives callers a concrete type to work with. This page explains the analyzed component instead of treating the directory name as an architectural boundary.

## Architecture

The CService implementation in c/service.c is a leaf with no recorded dependency edges. Its lifecycle is local: a caller reaches the service type, uses its fields or methods, and remains within this source file.

## Responsibilities

CService owns the native service representation. The [Native module](Native.md) supplies the parent architectural context.

documents.Native:
# Native

## Purpose

Native groups the C, CSharp, Cpp, Go, and Rust implementations into the native subsystem. It gives the language-specific leaf pages a shared architectural context while keeping source behavior in those child pages.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C --> Native
  CSharp --> Native
  Cpp --> Native
  Go --> Native
  Rust --> Native
```

The [C](C.md), [C#](C_.md), [C++](C__.md), [Go](Go.md), and [Rust](Rust.md) pages describe the native service surface and its language-specific implementations.

## Responsibilities

Native defines the grouping and navigation relationship for these implementations; it does not duplicate their leaf-level source explanations.
documents.JVM:
# JVM

## Purpose

JVM groups the Java, Kotlin, and Scala service implementations into a subsystem organized around the JVM language family. Its page explains the shared architecture while the children retain language-specific source details.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Java --> JVM
  Kotlin --> JVM
  Scala --> JVM
```

Read the [Java](Java.md), [Kotlin](Kotlin.md), and [Scala](Scala.md) pages for the concrete components and source paths.

## Responsibilities

JVM provides subsystem context and navigation for the three implementations without replacing their leaf documentation.

# Scripting

## Purpose

Scripting groups the JavaScript, PHP, Python, Ruby, and TypeScript service implementations into one scripting subsystem. The overview describes their shared role and directs readers to the language-specific pages for behavior.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  JavaScript --> Scripting
  PHP --> Scripting
  Python --> Scripting
  Ruby --> Scripting
  TypeScript --> Scripting
```

The [JavaScript](JavaScript.md), [PHP](PHP.md), [Python](Python.md), [Ruby](Ruby.md), and [TypeScript](TypeScript.md) pages provide the source-grounded details.

## Responsibilities

Scripting defines the parent navigation and explains how the language-specific services form one architectural family.
documents.Platform:
# Platform

## Purpose

Platform is the top-level subsystem that organizes native, JVM, and scripting implementations under one repository architecture. It connects the family overviews without repeating the source explanations owned by its children.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Native --> Platform
  JVM --> Platform
  Scripting --> Platform
```

The [Native](Native.md), [JVM](JVM.md), and [Scripting](Scripting.md) pages explain the three architectural branches and link onward to their language-specific leaves.

## Responsibilities

Platform provides repository navigation and the high-level relationship among implementation families.

overview:
# Replay Wiki

## Purpose

This fixture repository demonstrates a cross-language service platform. The wiki organizes the analyzed implementations by architectural family so a reader can move from the end-to-end repository shape to a language-specific source page without mistaking directories for behavior.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  caller --> Platform
  Platform --> Native
  Platform --> JVM
  Platform --> Scripting
```

The [Platform](Platform.md) page is the starting point for the top-level architecture. It links to the [Native](Native.md), [JVM](JVM.md), and [Scripting](Scripting.md) overviews, which in turn link to the leaf pages and their source-grounded explanations.

## Responsibilities

This repository overview explains navigation, subsystem relationships, and the boundary between architecture pages and implementation pages.
